newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait share index recovers slightly, up 2.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait share index recovers slightly, up 2.1 pct.

text.p: Kuwait's share index regained almost half of last week's losses, rising 2.1 percent to 1,869.2 points.

Last week the index fell 4.5 percent due to repeated statements of concern over regional stability. Washington said non-Arab Iran and former Kuwait occupier Iraq sought control of the region's oil, over two thirds of global reserves.
In recent weeks Kuwait has repeatedly said that Iraq was still a threat.
"These remarks are not helping," said a Gulf Arab official. "Investors get scared and many Kuwaitis and Gulf Arabs think twice before sending money into Kuwait."
Despite the rise in the index in the five-day week ending on Wednesday, the value and volume of traded shares fell, a weekly stock market report showed.
Value and volume for the week fell to 74 million dinars ($247.5 million) and 312 million shares from 108.8 million dinars and 377.4 million shares the previous week respectively.
Kuwait's financial standing has been improving since the 1991 Gulf War. On Thursday it completed payment on schedule of a $5.5 billion sovereign loan and principle.
During the trading week, 11 concerns were unchanged while gainers led losers 34-4 compared to last week's 2-45.
Gulf Insurance Co recorded the largest gain, rising 50 fils to 600, while Kuwait Computer fell 18 fils to 110. There are 1,000 fils per dinar.
Banks were the most active sector in terms of traded value with 25.9 million dinars, followed by non-Kuwaiti concerns with 14.3 million and investment firms with 13.6 million.
Only nationals of Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Kuwait -- can trade on the exchange. Foreign residents can invest through mutual funds.
